note: Master Campania tour records. hubs = towns a product can be sold from. Reuse for Sorrento, Capri, Naples, Positano pages: copy the record, change city folder, keep facts and Verify flags.

tours.sub: Arab-Norman cloister, crypt and sacred-art museum
ov: The cathedral of St Andrew stands at the top of 57 steps in Piazza Duomo. One ticket covers the Cloister of Paradise, the Basilica of the Crucifix with the Diocesan Museum, and the crypt of St Andrew.
The cloister was built in 1266–68 as a burial ground for Amalfi’s nobles and has interlaced Arab-style arches.
tours.tnote: Some guides quote €4; confirm at the ticket desk. Child and reduced fares: Verify. No separate non-EU or Indian-passport rate is published; Verify.
inc: Basilica of the Crucifix and Diocesan Museum
hl: Crypt holding the relics of St Andrew
Fountain of Sant’Andrea in the square outside
hrs: Open daily. Some sources show the Diocesan Museum closed on Mondays; Verify.
Hours change by season (about 09:00 to 18:45 in spring and summer, shorter in winter). Verify on the day.
Right at opening, before cruise and coach groups arrive.
tours.meet: Piazza Duomo, 84011 Amalfi. Walk from the ferry pier and the SITA bus stop takes about 3 minutes.
acc: The cathedral sits above 57 steps; a step-free route exists for visitors with reduced mobility: Verify with the cathedral.
Easy walking inside, with uneven old floors in the cloister.
rules: Shoulders and knees must be covered.
Quiet during services; photography limits in the church: Verify.
know: Entry to the nave during services is free but does not include the cloister and museum.
Sold from: Amalfi, Positano, Sorrento and Salerno as a stop on a coast day.
Weddings are common in summer and can close parts of the cathedral for short periods.
tours.canc: Walk-in ticket paid at the desk. Group booking terms: Verify.
faq: The church is free to enter outside paid hours, but the cloister, crypt and museum need the €3 ticket.
Plan 45 to 60 minutes including the steps.
also: Valley of the Mills, short walk
See the town from the sea
why: Easy 1-hour add-on in the town centre for any coast day.
Low ticket price; works for every age and budget.
how: Pair with a Marina Grande walk and a coffee at the square.
Suggest the first hour of the day to avoid group traffic.

tours.sub: Moorish cloister, terraces and the Belvedere over the sea
tours.lang: Self-guided; free guided tours on set dates
ov: A 13th-century villa in Ravello’s main square, known for its Moorish cloister, tower and terraced gardens above the coast.
In summer the Belvedere terrace hosts the Ravello Festival concerts.
tours.tnote: Child and reduced fares: Verify. No separate non-EU or Indian-passport rate is published; Verify.
inc: Free guided visit on scheduled dates (official programme)
hl: Terrace views over the Gulf of Salerno
Ravello Cathedral 30 m from the gate (free)
hrs: Open daily; the villa has opened later on special event mornings (for example 11 August 2026).
Hours are seasonal and extend in summer. Festival period 4 July to 5 September 2026 can change closing time. Verify.
Early morning, or late afternoon in summer.
tours.meet: Piazza Duomo, 84010 Ravello. Reached by SITA bus from Amalfi (about 25 minutes, Verify) or private transfer. The coach stop is a short walk from the square.
acc: Many steps and uneven paths; not suitable for wheelchairs on most routes: Verify.
know: Ravello is a hill town; allow transfer time from the coast.
Sold from: Amalfi, Positano, Sorrento and Salerno.
Combine with Villa Cimbrone, a 10-minute walk along Via Santa Chiara.
tours.canc: Walk-in ticket paid at the gate. Group booking terms: Verify.
faq: On dates in the official programme the guided visit needs only the entry ticket.
Is the villa open during the festival?
Yes, but closing times can change in July to September. Check the day.
why: Classic postcard stop on every Ravello day.
Fixed low ticket price makes group costing simple.
how: Sell it as a pair with Villa Cimbrone.
Recommend an early visit in summer to avoid heat and queues.

tours.t: Villa Cimbrone Gardens & Terrace of Infinity
tours.sub: Ravello’s clifftop gardens above the sea
ov: Gardens beside a hotel estate on the cliff above Ravello, ending at the Terrace of Infinity with a line of busts facing the sea.
Allow time: the grounds are larger than Villa Rufolo.
tours.tnote: Guides quote €7 to €10; confirm at the gate. Reduced fares: Verify.
hl: Rose garden and temple of Bacchus
hrs: Hours are seasonal; Verify at the gate or with the estate.
tours.meet: Via Santa Chiara 26, 84010 Ravello. About 10 minutes on foot from Piazza Duomo.
acc: Paths with steps and slopes; limited step-free access: Verify.
know: The estate is also a hotel, so some areas are private.
Sold from: Amalfi, Positano, Sorrento and Salerno.
faq: Is it the same as Villa Rufolo?
No. They are separate villas with separate tickets, a 10-minute walk apart.
The Terrace of Infinity, ideally early.
why: Quieter and more scenic than the main square sights.
Good for slower, photo-focused groups.
how: Pair with Villa Rufolo on a half-day Ravello visit.
Warn guests about the walk from the bus stop.

tours.sub: Boat-in sea cave at Conca dei Marini
tours.entry: Ticket at cave or with boat transfer
tours.closed: Open daily; closes in rough seas
ov: A small sea cave about 5 km west of Amalfi, lit green by sunlight through an underwater opening. You tour it in a rowboat that holds around 20 people.
You can reach it by lift and stairs from the coast road, or by boat from Amalfi.
tiers: Boat transfer from Amalfi (excludes cave entry)
tours.tnote: Sources quote €5, €6, €7 and €10 for the cave. Boat transfers sold separately from cave entry. Verify before quoting.
hl: Green light effect, strongest around midday
hrs: Open daily; closes when the sea is rough.
About 10:00 to 16:30 as a rule; the boat transfer runs roughly March to November. Verify.
Around midday for the brightest colour.
tours.meet: Conca dei Marini, SS163 (about 5 km from Amalfi). Boats leave from Molo Pennello, Amalfi. By land: stairs or lift from the car park on the coast road.
acc: Stairs or lift to the pier; boarding a rowboat needs steady balance. Not suitable for wheelchair users: Verify.
know: Many coast boat tours stop outside but exclude the cave ticket.
Sold from: Amalfi, Positano and Sorrento (boat tours).
Tip expected by boatmen: Verify.
tours.canc: Weather closures follow the operator’s terms. Verify.
faq: Is the cave ticket in the boat tour price?
What if the sea is rough?
Access can close without notice, so keep a flexible plan.
why: Short, low-cost highlight for a free half-day.
Strong photo moment for family groups.
how: State clearly that cave entry is extra.
Offer a Plan B for rough-sea days.
tours.mini: Entry or boat voucher after booking

tours.t: Amalfi Coast Boat Tour (Shared or Private)
tours.sub: Coastal cruise past Amalfi, Positano and coves
tours.entry: Boat departure at a set port
ov: Boat trips along the coast with stops at coves and villages such as Amalfi and Positano. Some itineraries continue to Capri.
Duration, route and port depend on the boat and the day’s sea conditions, so the final boarding point is confirmed at booking.
tiers: Private boat (per boat, not per person)
tours.tnote: All figures are reseller prices and need confirmation. Port fees, drinks and cave entry vary by boat.
inc: Drinks and swim stop (varies by boat)
steps: Meet at the port
Boarding point is confirmed with the booking.
Cruise the coast
Stops follow the booked itinerary and the sea.
Return to port
Back in the late afternoon on longer trips.
hrs: Runs by season and sea conditions.
Departure times set by operator. Verify.
tours.meet: Departure from Amalfi, Salerno, Positano or Sorrento area by boat base; the exact port is confirmed at booking.
acc: Boarding a small boat needs steady balance. Reduced mobility: ask before booking.
know: Sea conditions and the captain’s decision can change or cancel a trip.
Sold from: Amalfi, Positano, Sorrento, Salerno, Naples (by boat base).
Tell the operator about children and mobility needs in advance.
tours.canc: Weather cancellations follow each operator’s terms. Verify.
faq: Shared is cheaper; private lets you set the route and pace.
Only on itineraries that say so.
Varies by boat. Check the tour inclusions.
why: Best-selling way to see the coast with no road traffic.
Private boats suit family and VIP groups.
how: Ask for departure town first, then choose the fleet.
Quote private boats per boat, not per person.

tours.t: Path of the Gods Hike (Bomerano to Nocelle)
ov: A high trail along the cliffs above Praiano and Positano with wide views of the coast and Capri. The usual route runs from Bomerano (Agerola) to Nocelle.
The route has no ticket. Guided and transfer-inclusive versions are sold by operators.
tours.tnote: Transfers and guide prices vary by operator. Verify.
hl: Views of Capri and the Li Galli islands
steps: Reach Bomerano
Bus or transfer to the start in Agerola.
Walk the trail
Mostly level with some climbs; carry water.
Finish at Nocelle
Onward by bus or steps down to Positano (long, steep stairs).
hrs: Walk in daylight. Avoid after heavy rain.
tours.meet: Start at Bomerano, Agerola (bus from Amalfi, Verify). End at Nocelle, above Positano.
acc: Strenuous for some guests: uneven stone and steps, no shade in places.
Not suitable for wheelchairs or strollers.
know: Take water and sun protection.
Descending from Nocelle to Positano is a long staircase; many guests take the bus.
Sold from: Amalfi, Positano and Sorrento (transfers).
tours.canc: Free to walk. Guided tour terms: Verify.
faq: Yes, the trail has no entry fee.
Moderate, with uneven ground; suited to active guests.
No, but a guide helps with transfers and route.
why: Free product that adds value to a long stay.
Good for fitter, repeat visitors.
how: Check mobility and footwear first.
Offer a guided version with transfers to add margin.

tours.sub: Medieval paper mill in the Valley of the Mills
ov: A museum in a 13th-century paper mill in the Valle dei Mulini, a 15-minute walk from Piazza Duomo. It shows how Amalfi produced paper and includes a working demonstration.
tours.tnote: Ticket price and demonstration times: Verify with the museum.
tours.meet: Valle dei Mulini, Amalfi, about 15 minutes’ walk from Piazza Duomo. Exact address: Verify.
acc: Uphill walk and stairs; accessibility: Verify.
know: Sold from: Amalfi only as a town add-on.
faq: In the Valley of the Mills, uphill from the town centre.
Handmade paper is sold on site: Verify.
why: Low-cost cultural stop for slower days.
how: Pair with the cathedral and a walk through the valley.

tours.t: Capri Day Trip (Ferry, Blue Grotto & Island)
tours.sub: Island day by ferry or boat tour
tours.entry: Ferry tickets and separate Blue Grotto entry
tours.closed: Weather dependent; Blue Grotto closes in swell
ov: Capri is reached by hydrofoil from Sorrento (about 20–25 minutes), Naples, or seasonally from Amalfi and Positano (about 50–60 minutes). Some operators run boat tours from Sorrento, Positano and Amalfi.
The tour boat does not enter the Blue Grotto. Visitors transfer to a small rowboat, and the cave entry is paid separately in cash at the grotto.
tiers: Blue Grotto admission (paid at cave, cash)
tours.tnote: Ferry fares, boat-tour prices and rowboat fees vary by operator and season. Verify each element.
inc: Blue Grotto admission (when bought at the cave)
Skipper and soft drinks (varies by operator)
exc: Blue Grotto rowboat and entry on most boat tours
Funicular, chairlift and taxis on Capri
steps: Cross to Capri
Ferry or boat from the departure port.
Choose the cave or the island loop
Blue Grotto queues can be long.
Free time on the island
Funicular to Capri town or bus to Anacapri.
Return crossing
Allow a buffer for the last ferry.
hrs: Ferry timetables are seasonal; Verify the last return.
Take an early crossing for the Blue Grotto.
tours.meet: Departure port depends on the product: Sorrento, Naples (Molo Beverello), Positano or Amalfi. Confirm at booking.
acc: Island has steep streets and steps; the funicular helps. Rowboat entry to the cave is not suitable for guests with limited mobility: Verify.
know: Rough seas can close the Blue Grotto.
Sold from: Sorrento, Naples, Positano, Amalfi and Salerno.
Keep a buffer for the last ferry back.
faq: Usually not. It is bought separately at the cave.
What if the grotto is closed?
Operators offer an island tour or a refund per their terms.
why: Highest-demand day trip across the region.
Fits every hub, so one product serves many hotels.
how: Ask where the guests sleep, then pick the shortest crossing.
Tell guests the grotto is a separate cash payment.

ov: The ancient Roman city buried by the eruption of AD 79. Since April the park uses time-slot entry with a daily cap of 20,000 visitors.
Choose the basic ticket for the main site or the Pompeii+ ticket to add the suburban villas and Boscoreale.
tiers: Pompeii+ (adds villas, Villa Regina, Boscoreale Antiquarium)
tours.tnote: Prices from the park’s notice effective 12 January 2026. Under 18 free; €2 for EU citizens aged 18–25; first Sunday of the month free (booking still needed, Verify). Indian passport holders pay the standard adult price; Verify.
inc: Suburban villas, Villa Regina, Boscoreale Antiquarium
Repeat entries over the validity period
exc: Audio guide (not sold by the park)
Transport from Naples, Sorrento or Amalfi
steps: Choose entrance
Porta Marina, Piazza Anfiteatro or Piazza Esedra.
Security check
Small bags only (30×30×15 cm).
Visit by time slot
Keep to your slot; some houses have reduced access from 1 November after 16:00.
hrs: Hours vary by season; slots are sold online. Verify on the official site.
Opening time; heat peaks midday in summer.
tours.meet: Entrances at Porta Marina, Piazza Anfiteatro and Piazza Esedra. Circumvesuviana to Pompei Scavi–Villa dei Misteri. Official info line: +39 081 8575 347.
acc: Uneven Roman paving; some routes are accessible; Verify.
rules: Bags larger than 30×30×15 cm are not allowed.
know: Tickets are sold by the official seller; unofficial sites resell at higher prices.
Sold from: Naples, Sorrento, Amalfi, Positano and Salerno.
Hat, water and flat shoes are essential.
tours.canc: Official tickets: terms Verify. Reseller tours follow their own terms.
faq: The basic ticket is €20 and Pompeii+ is €25.
Are there tickets for non-EU visitors?
No separate rate; the standard adult price applies.
Three to four hours for the highlights.
why: Top-selling archaeology product for Indian groups from every hub.
Clear published fares make costing simple.
how: Quote slots early in peak season.
Add a licensed guide for first-time visitors.

ov: A trail leads to the crater rim of Vesuvius, with views over the Bay of Naples. Operators sell entry with a shuttle from Ercolano or other pickup points.
The summit can close in storms or high wind.
tiers: Entry + Vesuvio Express shuttle from Ercolano (reseller)
tours.tnote: Official park fare not confirmed. Reseller figures need checking.
hl: Views over the Bay of Naples
tours.meet: Pickup points vary by product (Ercolano, Pompeii, Naples, hotel). Confirm at booking.
acc: Steep gravel path; not suitable for wheelchairs: Verify.
know: Weather closures reduce the refund; check each operator.
Sold from: Naples, Sorrento, Amalfi, Positano and Salerno.
tours.canc: Operator terms; partial refund on weather closures at some resellers: Verify.
faq: Moderate; steep gravel for about 25 minutes (Verify).
why: Strong add-on for archaeology days.
how: Check footwear and mobility.
Offer a combo with Herculaneum.

tours.sub: Compact Roman town with well-preserved houses
ov: A smaller Roman town buried by the same eruption, with two-storey houses, mosaics and wooden structures preserved. Easier to cover than Pompeii.
tours.tnote: Reseller listings quote €16 adult, €2 for EU citizens aged 18–25, free under 18. Verify with the park. No separate non-EU or Indian-passport rate found; Verify.
tours.meet: Ercolano Scavi station on the Circumvesuviana, about 10 minutes’ walk to the entrance. Verify.
acc: Uneven paving; some accessible routes: Verify.
know: Sold from: Naples, Sorrento, Amalfi and Salerno.
Shorter than Pompeii, so it fits half-day plans.
faq: Better preserved and quicker to see.
Helpful; none is provided by the park.
why: Alternative for guests short on time.
how: Sell as a half-day with Vesuvius.

tours.sub: Greek temples and a national museum
tours.lang: No internal guided tours by the park
ov: Three Greek temples stand beside the National Archaeological Museum of Paestum. One ticket covers the Paestum site, the museum and the Velia site and is valid for 3 days.
The parks do not run internal guided tours; guides are arranged separately.
tours.tnote: Adult price not confirmed; Verify on the official site.
hrs: Regulation to 21 September 2026 published; later hours Verify. Ticket office 08:30–18:30, museum last admission 19:00 (summer).
tours.meet: Main entrance ticket office near the Temple of Neptune, Paestum.
acc: Museum fully accessible and linked to the site by an accessible route (official).
rules: No flash photography in the museum.
know: Sold from: Salerno, Amalfi and Naples.
About 1–1.5 hours by road from Amalfi: Verify.
faq: How many days is the ticket valid?
Three days, one entry to each site.
The park offers none; book one separately.
why: Quieter archaeology alternative with Greek temples.
how: Pair with a mozzarella tasting stop (Verify).

ov: A local experience in the terraced lemon groves of the coast with tastings. Duration, route and price depend on the operator.
tours.tnote: Price and inclusions: Verify with the operator.
tours.meet: Meeting point set by operator. Verify.
know: Sold from: Amalfi, Positano and Sorrento.
faq: Lemon tastings are normally vegetarian; Verify.
why: Easy cultural add-on that suits vegetarian groups.
how: Confirm transfer and dietary needs.

tours.t: Private Car & Minivan Tour of the Amalfi Coast
tours.sub: Chauffeur-driven day to Positano, Amalfi and Ravello
ov: A private car or minivan with a driver for the coast road, with stops at viewpoints and towns such as Positano, Amalfi and Ravello.
Stops, timing and pace are set when you book.
tours.tnote: Pricing per vehicle by route and duration: Quote on request.
hl: Photo stops on the coast road
tours.meet: Pickup at hotel, port or station, agreed at booking.
acc: Vehicle access varies; mobility needs should be stated at booking.
know: The coast road is slow in summer.
Sold from: all hubs.
faq: Yes, the vehicle is reserved for your group.
Can we add Pompeii or Paestum?
Yes; route and price are quoted.
Driver only unless a guide is added: Verify.
why: Flexible for families and small groups.
how: Quote per vehicle and ask for the hotel address.

tours.sub: Seasonal sea links along the coast
ov: Passenger ferries link Salerno, Amalfi, Positano and Capri in the warmer months, and Sorrento to Capri runs more often. Amalfi to Capri takes about 50–60 minutes, often via Positano.
Timetables and fares change by season.
tours.tnote: Fares and timetables: Verify with the operator.
tours.meet: Amalfi and Positano piers; Salerno, Sorrento and Naples ports. Confirm at booking.
know: Rough seas cancel crossings.
Sold from: all hubs.
faq: Coast links are seasonal; Verify the dates.
About 50–60 minutes from Amalfi, 20–25 from Sorrento.
why: Useful for hotel-to-hotel moves without a car.
how: Check the last return time before selling.
